newsitem.title: USA: FBI publicly seeks assistance in tobacco probe.
newsitem.headline: FBI publicly seeks assistance in tobacco probe.

text.p: The FBI said Thursday it is seeking the assistance of current or former tobacco company officials in the continuing Justice Department criminal investigation involving the industry.

In a posting to the FBI's Web site, the FBI and the Justice Department said they are conducting a probe to determine whether any federal criminal laws had been violated by tobacco industry corporations, employees or representatives.

The FBI said it is seeking help from "past or present tobacco company researchers, scientists, product development personnel or manufacturing officials knowledgeable about the cigarette development and manufacuting process."
It said the assistance could be provided confidentially.

The FBI said the probe is looking into allegations that industry representatives made false or misleading statements to Congress and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration about tobacco, nicotine, cigarettes, the cigarette manufacturing process and the manipulation of nicotine.

Department officials said the request for help should be publicised in Richmond, Va.; Louisville, Ky.; Winston-Salem, N.C.; and Macon, Ga. -- cities with a high concentration of current or former tobacco industry employees.

The plea for assistance was unusual in that the FBI and the Justice Department rarely comment on pending investigations. The probe is being run by prosecutors from the Justice Department's fraud section, assisted by FBI agents.
No charges have yet been brought in the long-running probe, but sources close to the investigation have predicted that indictments could come later this year.
